The unit turns on whether lowercasing changes how the configured models follow the prompts, and the supplied sources do not show that it does. sources.json found no Anthropic statement on all-caps wording and no restatement of the dial-back advice for the 5.x models (not_found, Q1). It also found no GPT-5.x or GPT-6 guidance on emphatic wording beyond the GPT-5 Cursor example (not_found, Q3). S1's advice concerns tool and skill over-triggering on Opus 4.5 and 4.6. S9 concerns a capitalized thoroughness instruction on GPT-5. The workers here run Opus 5.5 and GPT-6-Astra (README:41-45). S5 says emphasis spread over many lines loses force, not that it causes the model to misread the instruction. These capitals mark scope and quantifiers that mean the same in lowercase. Under the rule to judge wording on following rather than style, the edit is a style change with no shown behavioral benefit. Keeping the text is the better-supported outcome, and B's cited sources check out.

The refuter could check those values, so they were not unverifiable. B says a null field means unknown and keeps verified falsehoods refutable. B also avoids A's wording that an unverifiable license is 'corrected'. A's comment change exists only as the X7 note's description, with no text and a pointer to :256, which is an assertion. It therefore cannot be applied exactly as written. Neither sentence contains a banned license phrase (test :259-261). B loosely credits the null-field exception to 'the selection principles', whose nearest rule is 'a missing result is pending, never refuted'. That does not change behavior and does not block B.

items.reasons: Both returns rightly replace an instruction to run `/mcp` and `/context`, which the model cannot type. S6 recognizes a command only at the start of the user's message, and the installed Skill description excludes built-in CLI commands. The repository also runs these commands in the interactive client (recipes/claude-native-profile.md:272-273; docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md:110-111). The fallback decides the unit. CLAUDE.md also loads in default workflow children (workflows README:249) and in headless runs, where no user can answer. AGENTS.md:15 allows stopping only for sign-in, OS consent or an unresolved material decision. A says 'report it as unconfirmed and name the command that would'. That works in all of these settings and leaves an unknown unknown. B says 'ask for the relevant ... output', which assumes a user is present. B also names a `/plugin` command that neither the repository nor the supplied sources document, and it is twice as long in a file that is always loaded. B's broader component list (agents, per T1) and its caveat about Skill are sound. A leaves out agents, but that can only produce an unconfirmed report, never a false claim that a plugin is active. The preference for A is therefore moderate.
